about: Your stock-picking strategies. Each runs every Sunday on SEC-filing data (screens.py). Picks are logged with that day's prices to strategies/ledger.jsonl and scored against the S&P 500 (SPY) after 13, 26 and 52 weeks. A strategy is frozen once created: to change one, add a new version with a new id and keep the old one running. Filters use fields from screens.py: revenue, roe, margin, de, cr, epsTTM, epsYr, epsQ, salesQ, eps5y, pe, pb, mktCap, beta, momentum, chg52.

strategies.name: Buffett-style: cheap, safe, high quality, large
strategies.description: Based on Frazzini, Kabiller & Pedersen, 'Buffett's Alpha' (2018): Berkshire's returns are explained by owning cheap, safe (low-beta), high-quality, large companies, plus leverage (not used here). Quality = profitable, growing, low debt. Cheap = low price-to-book. Safe = low beta vs the S&P 500. Ranked on all three equally; top 10, at most 3 from any one industry (SEC industry code), so it can't turn into an insurance fund.
